body.statement: The compatible causal set is exactly \(Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U]\). If the complete procedure of Ejaz and Bareinboim returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) for this fixed query and \(F\) is nonconstant, then \([L,U]\) is a strict informative refinement of that nonidentification report because it gives every and only compatible values. If \(F\) is constant, then \(L=U\), so the result is point identification and agrees with their identified-case conclusion; the absence of \(rstar\) alone does not imply that their complete procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).
body.justification: The theorem reports the exact relational compatibility range and sharpens a failure report only on instances where the complete comparator procedure actually fails.
body.gap: Ejaz and Bareinboim establish a complete identification procedure and neural extrema correctness but do not return the sharp compatible set when that procedure returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).
body.consumer: Experiment 6.1 can accompany its N3 fitted point with the certified population range; for its documented clamped count query, the theorem reduces to the known logical range \([0,1]\).
body.proof_tex:
The inclusion \(\Theta\subseteq F([0,1])\) follows immediately from the polynomial-reduction lemma: each \(M\in Mone\) has a shared scalar \(q_M\in[0,1]\) and \(Q(M)=F(q_M)\).

For the reverse inclusion, fix \(q_0\in[0,1]\).  For every endogenous type \(t\), collect \(0\), \(1\), and all cumulative probabilities of all explicit source rows of type \(t\); for the free binary row also collect \(q_0\).  Order the distinct numbers as
\[
 0=b_{t,0}<b_{t,1}<\cdots<b_{t,h_t}=1.
\]
Let a type-\(t\) noise variable have atom \(j\) with mass \(b_{t,j}-b_{t,j-1}>0\).  For a context \(c\), define the common type mechanism on atom \(j\) to be the category selected by any point of \((b_{t,j-1},b_{t,j})\) under the cumulative row for \(c\).  No cumulative threshold lies in the interior of this interval, so the category is well defined.  Summing the masses of the intervals assigned to a category gives exactly its row probability.  Give distinct ground nodes independent copies of the appropriate type noise, and use a fixed point-mass row at contexts absent from both sources and the target.

This is a finite-noise model with type-shared mechanisms.  Topological induction on each acyclic source grounding shows that its conditional row at every positive-probability source context is the recovered row.  Its source joint law is consequently the product of those conditionals, which equals the corresponding member of \(Psrc\) by source compatibility.  Zero-probability source contexts do not affect that joint law.  In the target the free row is \((1-q_0,q_0)\); the polynomial-reduction calculation therefore gives \(Q(M_{q_0})=F(q_0)\).  All defining clauses of \(Mone\) hold, so \(M_{q_0}\in Mone\).  Hence \(F([0,1])\subseteq\Theta\).

It remains to identify the endpoints.  A polynomial is continuous.  For completeness, compact attainment can be seen without an extra hypothesis: choose points whose values approach the supremum of \(F([0,1])\), repeatedly bisect \([0,1]\) and retain a half containing infinitely many chosen points, and use completeness of the real numbers to obtain a common limit point; continuity gives a maximizer.  The same construction gives a minimizer.  If an optimizer \(c\) is interior, then for \(h>0\) and \(h<0\) the difference quotients \((F(c+h)-F(c))/h\) have opposite weak signs; their common limit is therefore \(F'(c)=0\).  Thus every optimizer lies in \(Ccrit\).  By the definitions of \(L\) and \(U\), the attained minimum and maximum are \(L\) and \(U\).

Finally, if \(y\) lies between \(L\) and \(U\), take optimizer locations \(c_-\) and \(c_+\), order the interval between them, and bisect it while retaining a half whose endpoint values bracket \(y\).  The nested intervals have a common point \(c\), and continuity gives \(F(c)=y\).  Consequently \(F([0,1])=[L,U]\), and hence \(\Theta=[L,U]\).

If \(F\) is nonconstant and the stipulated complete comparator returns \(\mathsf{FAIL}\), that output supplies no compatible value, whereas \([L,U]\) supplies exactly all compatible values by the equality just proved; this is the asserted strict informational refinement of the report.  If \(F\) is constant, every compatible model has the same value and \(L=U\), so the query is point identified.  The mere presence of an unsupported row cannot force failure: for example, a graph may contain a target-relevant binary node using \(rstar\) upstream of an outcome whose supported conditional success probability is \(1/2\) for both values of that node.  Then \(F(q)=1/2\) although \(rstar\) remains unrestricted.  A complete identification procedure must classify this query as identified, establishing the final qualification.
